summary.text: Leroy Comrie is the Democratic incumbent for New York State Senate District 14 in southeast Queens and is running unopposed in the general election.

A lifelong South Queens resident and former community school board president, he served twelve years on the New York City Council before his 2014 election to the Senate, where he chairs the Committee on Corporations, Authorities and Commissions.

paragraphs.text: Comrie was born in New York City to Ruby Frith-Comrie and Leroy Comrie Sr., immigrants from Jamaica, and grew up in the South Queens communities he now represents.
He attended P.S. 116, I.S. 8 and Jamaica High School, then the University of Bridgeport, where his official biography says he developed his interest in politics and government.
He was elected president of his local community school board before becoming a public official.
Comrie served twelve years on the New York City Council, from 2002 to 2013, representing a southeast Queens district.
He was Deputy Majority Leader and Chairman of the Queens Delegation and chaired the Rules, Consumer Affairs and Land Use committees.
His official biography lists among his Council accomplishments increasing senior tax exemptions, creating the city's first foreclosure prevention program and curtailing payday loans.
In 2013 he launched a campaign for Queens Borough President but dropped out before the primary and endorsed Melinda Katz.

Comrie was elected to the State Senate in 2014, defeating incumbent Malcolm Smith and Munir Avery in the Democratic primary and running unchallenged in the general election, and assumed office on January 1, 2015.
The district includes parts of Jamaica, Cambria Heights, Queens Village, Hollis, St. Albans, Laurelton, Jamaica Estates, Briarwood, Hillcrest and Kew Gardens.

He chairs the Senate Committee on Corporations, Authorities and Commissions, as he described in a November 2025 PoliticsNY Q&A, and he is a member of the Budget and Revenue, Finance, Procurement and Contracts, Racing, Gaming and Wagering, and Rules committees and the Select Majority Task Force on Minority and Women-Owned Business Enterprises.
He was appointed to the Public Authorities Control Board in 2019 and was named a 2026 New York State Senate Veterans' Hall of Fame Honoree.

According to his official biography, Comrie is a member of the Black, Puerto Rican, Hispanic and Asian Legislative Caucus and a lifelong member of Saint Albans the Martyr Episcopal Church, and he has been married to Marcia Moxam since 1990; they have two adult children.
